correctness.rationale: The proof is an iff classification. If the center is absent, domination is equivalent to meeting every blade and perfect matching reduces to even order in each selected clique. If the center is present, any perfect matching uses the center in exactly one blade, after which all remaining blade components must have even order; equivalently exactly one selected blade count is odd. Both converses are explicit. The enumerator follows from the even/odd subset polynomials. The packaged exhaustive checker independently validates every subset for eight small parameter pairs.

value.rationale: The result gives a natural complete classification and the entire paired-domination polynomial for a standard infinite graph family, strictly refining the known scalar minimum. The two-case parity rule exposes how the universal cut vertex controls perfect matching feasibility across blades and yields immediate exact corollaries for every cardinality, the number of minima, and the total count.
